demographics.trauma_type: Accidentally caused serious injury to another

Triggers.value: Physical pain in a part of the body

Threat.value: I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place
I watch other people closely for signs that they might harm me
Even when others tell me I am safe I find it impossible to believe it

Memory.value: When memories come to mind of what happened, I feel my body is in the same position as when the frightening event occurred.
When I remember the event I feel intense rage
When I remember the event I feel overwhelming grief

Negative Appraisals.value: There is something about me that made the event happen
I am no longer capable of doing the things that defined me

issues.item: Threat from Strangers: I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations
issues.explanation: For trauma involving accidentally causing serious injury to another person, the threat profile is not clinically coherent: fearing harm from strangers in ordinary situations and scanning others for signs they might attack suggests an interpersonal-victimization or assault-based danger schema, which is hard to reconcile with the rest of this profile. The listed triggers center on pain, victim reminders, and proximity, and the appraisals center on guilt, incompetence, and loss of self-trust rather than danger from other people.

issues.item: Watching Others: I watch other people closely for signs that they might harm me
issues.explanation: The memory item of intense rage on recall is also a poor fit with the surrounding profile. In accidental-injury trauma with strong guilt/grief appraisals, grief on recall is coherent, but rage lacks a clear target and is not supported by the rest of the nodes. Combined with the stranger-threat items, it pulls the profile toward an anger/hostility or assault formulation that is not reflected in the triggers or appraisals.
